exposure: Fetal abdominal needle insertion angle for radiofrequency ablation (RFA)
Fetal dorsal needle insertion angle for RFA
outcome: Duration of pregnancy post-RFA (time from RFA to delivery)
cohort: The study included 56 women with complicated monochorionic multiple pregnancies who underwent selective reduction using radiofrequency ablation (RFA) with either abdominal or dorsal needle insertion angles.
finding: There were no significant differences in perinatal outcomes between fetal abdominal and dorsal needle insertion angles for radiofrequency ablation (RFA), and the overall live birth rate was 73.5%.
gest_age: Mean gestation at birth was 31.6 ± 6.5 weeks; gestational age at RFA was a predictor of the duration of pregnancy post-RFA.
